name: House Oversight Committee

summary.text: The U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform describes itself as the principal oversight committee of the House, with legislative jurisdiction over the District of Columbia, federal procurement, federal personnel systems and the Postal Service, and oversight jurisdiction that its website says covers virtually everything government does; House Rule X allows it to investigate any matter at any time. On this site it appears through its 2025 subpoena and release of records from Jeffrey Epstein's estate and as the recipient of the Senate Finance Committee ranking member's June 2026 referral on Leon Black's Epstein ties.

facts.claim: The committee's website states that it has legislative jurisdiction over the District of Columbia, the government procurement process, federal personnel systems and the Postal Service, and that its primary responsibility is oversight of virtually everything government does.
facts.quote: its primary responsibility is oversight of virtually everything government does

facts.claim: Under its 119th Congress rules the committee has seven subcommittees, including Health Care and Financial Services (covering monetary policy, banking and tax policy) and Delivering on Government Efficiency (covering the federal civil service and government reorganizations).
facts.quote: Committee on Oversight and Government Reform 119th Congress Rule 1 — General

facts.claim: In 2025 the committee released records obtained from Jeffrey Epstein's estate under an August 25, 2025 subpoena, including a further 20,000 pages on November 12, 2025 comprising court records, financial documents, text messages and emails; Chairman Comer said the committee had obtained information about Epstein's bank accounts and would pursue those records.
facts.quote: The Committee also obtained information about Epstein's bank accounts. The Committee will pursue these bank records.
